predecessors.note: Wang Shenzhi took Fuzhou in summer 893 as acting governor and was made Weiwu jiedushi c. 898 (Wang Shenzhi page); the Min page says the kingdom existed 'between the years of 909 and 945'.

'The Wuyue secured the area around Fuzhou' and 'Fuzhou joined the Wuyue domain as a vassal'; Wuyue forces arrived in winter 946 and spring 947 (Southern Tang page), after the end of Min.

'Control over the coastal prefectures of Quanzhou and Zhangzhou by Liu Congxiao was recognized' by the Southern Tang as Qingyuan Jiedushi (Southern Tang page); a vassal of the Southern Tang until the Song.

capitals.note: 'Its capital was Fuzhou' (no years on the page). Wang Yanzheng's Yin ruled from Jianzhou in 943-945; the Wang Yanzheng page makes Fu the southern capital.

The Min page says the kingdom lasted 'between the years of 909 and 945' and sat in 'a mountainous region of modern-day Fujian province'. The page names Fu Prefecture, not the province's boundary.

ledger.note: 944: Zhang, Quan and Ting side with Yin. 'Zhang, Quan, and Ting had all submitted to Yin' (the page's 944 narrative, undated within the year); Liu Congxiao's Quan officers joined Yin. Only Fuzhou stays with the Min court of Zhu Wenjin, who had assassinated Wang Xi in 944.

945: Wang Yanzheng reunites Min under his rule. 'By February 945 Wang Yanxin [Yanxi] had died and Wang Yanzheng reunited Min'; the Wang Yanzheng infobox: Yin to 'February or March 945', Min reign 'February or March 945 - October 2, 945'. The page is thin on Fuzhou: Wu Chengyi was let into the city after Lin Renhan's uprising, undated.

ledger.note: 945: Min ends. Wang Yanzheng's Min reign ends 'October 2, 945' (infobox); the Southern Tang page: after Jianzhou fell 'the majority of Min territory' was under Southern Tang rule. Fuzhou goes to Li Renda and then to Wuyue as a vassal (winter 946-spring 947), Quan and Zhang to Liu Congxiao's Qingyuan.

wars.name: Min-Southern Han border fighting
wars.outcome: No border moved: a Min ambush at Meikou in 922 failed because Liu Yan left; in 924 'A Min counterattack defeated Southern Han forces, however', and Liu Yan withdrew.

wars.outcome: Wang Yanzheng's Yin held Jian from 943 and Zhang, Quan and Ting from 944; Wang Xi was assassinated by Zhu Wenjin in 944; Wang Yanzheng reunited Min by February 945.
wars.note: 'Later in 941, Wang Xi claimed imperial title and resumed his campaign against Wang Yanzheng, but the battles were indecisive.' The Min page lists the 'Independence of Yin (943-945)'.

wars.name: Southern Tang conquest of Min

wars.outcome: Southern Tang victory: Jianzhou fell on 2 October 945 and Wang Yanzheng was captured; the Southern Tang took Jian and Ting, Wuyue got Fuzhou as a vassal, Liu Congxiao kept Quan and Zhang as Qingyuan.
wars.note: The same page also says 'The campaign ended successfully late in 947', which conflicts with the October 945 fall; the Five Dynasties page says Southern Tang 'finished its conquest of Min in 945'. The page also calls Min 'conquered in 945' without a vassal relation.

certainty.note: The Fujian outline is a mountain-and-coast region without any treaty line on an opened page; the Yin split of 943-945 follows prefecture names (Jian, Zhang, Quan, Ting), not surveyed lines.

notes: Cliopatria's Min row (911-946, two identical 121,944 km2 shapes) is one state; its 946 year is after the end: Min ended on 2 October 945 and the land went to the Southern Tang (Jian, Ting), Wuyue (Fuzhou, as a vassal from winter 946-spring 947) and Qingyuan (Quan, Zhang). No pages give an infobox area; the shape equals 98 percent of modern Fujian's area, so the shape is plausible. This batch adds a rebel dossier yin-ten-kingdoms for Wang Yanzheng's Yin (943-945), a state no Cliopatria row covers, because the pages date it twice (Southern Tang page, Wang Yanzheng page, Min page 'Independence of Yin (943-945)'); the Min ledger's 943 and 944 losses and the 945 merge are its counterparts. Not recorded: the Min emperor Wang Yanjun's imperial claim (the Min page lists 'Wang Yanjun declared himself the Emperor' and the era names Longqi 933-935 and Yonghe 935, but gives no year for the title), so the ruler list is left out; the Min page's tree gives 'r. 939-944 Wang Yanzheng', which contradicts the Yin years. Nominal ties: Wang Shenzhi 'recognized the new emperor' of Later Liang and sent tribute by sea in 909-923, 'recognized Emperor Zhuangzong's suzerainty' in 923 (Wang Shenzhi page); the Wuyue marriage of 916; none of these is drawn as a vassal tint (the Five Dynasties page describes no general vassal system). The Wang Shenzhi page says Wang Shenzhi took Fuzhou in 893 and the five prefectures are never listed on any opened page; Ting, Zhang and Jian are read as Longyan, Zhangzhou and Nanping.
